desc: Filter the input `nums` to identify "small" numbers (≤ threshold) and "large" numbers (> threshold), noting that all large numbers form isolated components.
Initialize a Disjoint Set Union (DSU) structure for the indices of the "small" numbers (or map values to indices).

Iterate through every integer `i` from 1 to `threshold`: if `i` is present in the filtered "small" numbers, iterate through its multiples `j = 2*i, 3*i, ...` up to `threshold`; for each multiple `j` present in the array, perform a union operation between the sets containing `i` and `j`.
After processing all unions, count the number of unique root parents in the DSU structure for the "small" numbers.
Add the count of "large" numbers to the result from the previous step to get the total number of connected components.
Implement the `countComponents` method with the DSU logic: filter numbers, initialize DSU, iterate multiples to union sets, and count components.
Run unit tests against provided examples and edge cases.
Verify time complexity on maximum constraints ($N=10^5, T=2 \cdot 10^5$).
